instructions.negotiation:
Clients commonly ask to make attorneys’ fees mutual, or to make the provision mutual while limiting fee recovery to the prevailing party.

Making attorneys’ fees mutual gives both sides the same right to recover attorneys’ fees and related costs.

Making attorneys’ fees mutual and limiting recovery to the prevailing party means either side can recover fees, but only if that side prevails in the dispute.

We generally accommodate one of these approaches, especially as a concession when multiple redlines are requested.

concessions.description: Make attorneys’ fees mutual so either party has the same right to recover attorneys’ fees and related costs.

instructions.summary:
This says that if a client breaches non-solicitation, they owe Oceans a fee equal to 12 months of that Diver's billing rate, due within 10 days.

If either side breaches non-interference, they owe the other side 12 months of the affected relationship's revenue.

These are pre-agreed ("liquidated") damages, not just a starting point for a lawsuit, and either side can also seek a court order to stop the behavior, not just money.
This sets the official channels and addresses for formal legal notices between the parties (not day-to-day communication).

This says that each Diver has an Initial Term of 3 months, which auto-renews in further 3-month blocks unless someone ends it.

The client owes the full term's fees regardless of how much they actually use the Diver's time.

If a client ends things early during a renewal, they get a 50% rebate on the remaining months; if Oceans ends it early, the client only pays up to that point and gets a refund for anything overpaid.
This says that Oceans owns its own IP, the client owns theirs. Neither side's IP transfers to the other by default.

This is the core service: as long as the client pays and follows the contract, they get access to the Diver's services.

Access is for the client's own internal use only - not to resell or hand off to someone else.
This confirms Oceans and the client are independent businesses working together - not employer/employee, partners, or a joint venture.

This section explains that if a Diver can't work for over a month, or isn't a good fit during the Initial Term, the client can request a replacement. And Oceans has 15 business days to propose someone; if they miss that window, the client stops owing fees for that Diver.

It also explains that if Oceans proposes a replacement in time and the client says no, the client still owes the remaining fees for the term. And if a replacement is used, the client gets a service credit for the downtime, applied to future fees.

This means that Oceans has 15 business days to propose a suitable replacement. If we can’t, the buyer stops owing the remaining fees; if we do and they decline the replacement, they still owe the rest of the term.

They request the ability to cancel at any time for any reason and want the ability to reject a replacement for a full refund, or for the ability to veto the process outright and get a refund.

Services are provided "as-is" - Oceans doesn't promise any particular outcome or result.

Even though Divers are vetted and trained, Oceans doesn't guarantee a specific Diver will be the right fit - the client's only recourse if something's wrong is to request a replacement or terminate, not to claim damages.
